$comment: Mission 1.67 §9 and §53. Every first-party document request, including the ones that returned nothing. A redirect to irrelevant content and a 404 both spend budget.

search_navigation_requests.$comment: §7 and §41. Search engines were used for navigation only — to locate exact first-party paths rather than guess them, since a guessed path that 404s spends document budget. No gate is closed by a search result.

retrieval_summary_guard.$comment: §42. Mission 1.63's nonexistent sentence is the canonical negative control, and this mission met the shape twice.

instances.what_the_summary_reported: Substantive technical content — scanning engine minions and modules, output mangling, and host data up to six months — attributed to docs.binaryedge.io paths.
instances.what_the_live_documents_returned: Three separate paths on that host each 301-redirected to one non-technical Coalition customer notice, which itself returned HTTP 403.
instances.project_interpretation: The index a search engine holds is not the document the host currently serves. Nothing from that summary was used to close any gate.

instances.what_the_summary_reported: A confirmed_time field with an example timestamp, a banner search endpoint, and scan cadence figures.
instances.what_the_live_documents_returned: HTTP 403 on both attempted first-party documentation paths.
instances.project_interpretation: Recorded as documentation not retrievable from this environment. None of the summary's load-bearing wording was used, in either direction.
